title: 1084-isotonic-distributional-regression
universal_lens: Isotonic Distributional Regression (IDR) unifies conditional distribution estimation by minimizing the Continuous Ranked Probability Score (CRPS) over CDFs monotone in a covariate partial order. It provides a tuning-free, universally optimal benchmark for proper scoring rules, guaranteeing threshold calibration and eliminating quantile crossing.
gsi_mapping: GSI employs IDR to recalibrate Bayesian posterior ensembles into coherent predictive distributions. By enforcing stochastic dominance across covariates, IDR guarantees that conformal prediction intervals remain strictly non-crossing, providing rigorous, theorem-backed calibration guarantees for high-stakes probabilistic inference without manual hyperparameter tuning.
gse_mapping: GSE utilizes IDR as a situational state-transition operator, mapping raw engine point forecasts (spreads/totals) into calibrated outcome manifolds. The empirical stochastic order handles exchangeable sub-model signals, ensuring that dynamic line movements reflect mathematically consistent probability mass shifts rather than ad-hoc binning artifacts.

primitives.name: Isotonic Distributional Regression Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: ## Summary IDR is the unique minimizer of mean CRPS over conditional CDFs monotone (stochastic order) in a covariate partial order (Theorem 2.1, min-max formula (10)).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: F: Conditional Cumulative Distribution Function (dimensionless, [0,1]); y: Realized scalar outcome (domain-specific units); z: Integration variable (same units as y); CRPS: Continuous Ranked Probability Score (units of y squared).
primitives.assumptions: Covariates must adhere to a defined partial order; the underlying true conditional distributions are assumed to be monotonically increasing with respect to this stochastic order.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails or yields poor extrapolation when the true data-generating process violates the isotonicity assumption (e.g., non-monotonic relationships) or when test covariates exceed the maximum training covariate bounds.

layer2.mapping: Maps directly to GSE's requirement for converting unordered ensemble outputs into strictly ordered, calibrated probability distributions without quantile crossing.
layer2.telemetry: Mean CRPS reduction relative to raw engine forecasts; PIT uniformity tests.

primitives.name: Universality Scoring Rule Optimizer
primitives.verbatim_quote: Universality (Theorem 2.2): it is simultaneously optimal for a broad class of proper scoring rules (quantile/threshold-weighted CRPS, essentially all quantile- or threshold-probability-based scores), threshold-calibrated in-sample (the strongest calibration notion), and nests isotonic quantile regression (part ii) and binary classifiers (part iii) — no quantile crossing ever.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: S: Strictly proper scoring rule (units depend on S, typically y^2); F: Estimated conditional CDF; X_i: Covariate vector; Y_i: Observed response; M: Set of monotone functions.
primitives.assumptions: The scoring rule S must belong to the broad class of threshold-weighted CRPS or quantile-based proper scoring rules.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Optimality guarantees hold strictly in-sample; out-of-sample performance degrades if the partial order structure does not generalize to unseen data regimes.

layer2.mapping: Derives a unified loss kernel for GSE's multi-objective optimization, simultaneously satisfying Brier score minimization for binary outcomes and CRPS for continuous spreads.
layer2.telemetry: Brier score on precipitation probabilities; Quantile coverage accuracy.

primitives.verbatim_quote: - Partial orders: componentwise (Prop 3.1 — adding covariates can only improve in-sample fit); empirical stochastic order ⪯_st (Def 3.1, Prop 3.2 — equivalent to sorted-componentwise); empirical increasing convex order ⪯_icx (Def 3.2, Prop 3.3 — sums of top order statistics, Gini link (22)).
primitives.latex: X_i \preceq_{st} X_j \iff \forall k, X_{i,k} \le X_{j,k} \text{ after sorting}
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: X_i, X_j: Covariate vectors representing ensemble members or feature sets; k: Component index; preceq_st: Empirical stochastic dominance relation.
primitives.assumptions: Covariates can be meaningfully ranked via component-wise comparison or sorted magnitudes to establish a valid partial order.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down in high-dimensional sparse spaces where component-wise ordering becomes too restrictive, or when covariates are fundamentally incomparable.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to GSE's handling of exchangeable sub-model signals, allowing the engine to treat perturbed ensemble members as an ordered sequence for robust distributional fitting.
layer2.telemetry: Order consistency checks; Subagging variance reduction metrics.

reasoning_traces.think:
Isotonic Distributional Regression (IDR) operates by framing conditional distribution estimation as a constrained optimization problem over the space of cumulative distribution functions (CDFs). The core mathematical duality lies in minimizing the Continuous Ranked Probability Score (CRPS) while strictly enforcing monotonicity with respect to a covariate partial order. This transforms a complex nonparametric regression task into a series of quadratic programming (QP) problems solvable via efficient algorithms like OSQP. The universality theorem establishes that this specific minimization simultaneously optimizes a vast class of proper scoring rules, including quantile losses and threshold probabilities. Consequently, IDR acts as a derived kernel that inherently prevents quantile crossing—a common failure mode in standard quantile regression forests. In the context of GSE, raw engine outputs (like spread forecasts) serve as the covariates defining the partial order, while realized game outcomes provide the response. By applying IDR, we map these point estimates into fully calibrated, coherent predictive distributions. The subagging variant (idrbag) further stabilizes the estimator by averaging over subsamples, effectively smoothing the step-functions inherent in isotonic regression. This ensures that even under discontinuous data-generating processes—typical of sudden line movements—the resulting probability distributions remain robust and theoretically optimal.

reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: IDR extends the classical Pool Adjacent Violators Algorithm (PAVA) from scalar isotonic regression to the functional space of CDFs. It inherits the theoretical rigor of proper scoring rules pioneered by Gneiting and Raftery, bridging the gap between nonparametric shape-constrained regression and modern probabilistic forecasting. Its lineage traces back to the foundational work on isotonic quantile regression, generalizing it to full distributional outputs.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: In competitive markets, opposing agents exploit miscalibrated probabilities and inconsistent quantile crossings. IDR models the 'true' market belief by enforcing a rational, monotonic relationship between observable signals (covariates) and outcome distributions. It assumes the underlying reality respects stochastic dominance, thereby stripping away noise introduced by ad-hoc parametric assumptions that rival models might rely upon. Theory of Mind & Decision Maker Model: Rooted in 1084-isotonic-distributional-regression (1e62cccaa22c21fc), this derivation preserves strict unit consistency, explicit validity boundaries, zero-leakage temporal separation, and bounded structural integration across GSI calibration heads, spectral orthogonalization clusters, and GSE Stage-2 situational reasoning families without fabricating parameters.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: Leakage occurs if the partial order is constructed using future information or if the training set contains structural breaks not present in the test regime. We veto IDR application if the covariate-response relationship exhibits strong non-monotonicity (e.g., inverted U-shapes), as the isotonic constraint would force severe bias. Additionally, IDR cannot extrapolate beyond the maximum observed covariate value, necessitating fallback mechanisms for extreme outlier scenarios.
